claims.statement: The registered profile-sensitive rank inequality holds at every strict descent for all profiles with 1<=m<=45.
claims.scope: Finite exact computation over all 17,295 count triples with 1<=m<=45, scanning all strict forward differences of the actual parent with integer zero extension, including the terminal descent.
claims.reason: An independently written exact convolution scan reproduced 938,431 strict-descent rows and minimum slack 44; finite scope only.

claims.statement: For C=GQ, P=C+zL^(N+1), and E=(1+z)P'-(N+2)P, E=L^(N+1)-2zQ+G*sum_i(1-(r_i-1)z)H_i and [z^k]E=(k+1)P[k+1]-(N+2-k)P[k].
claims.scope: All finite ordinary profiles with r_i in {2,3,4}; polynomial identity over integers with zero-extended coefficients. The claim is only the identity; coefficientwise nonnegativity of E at forbidden ranks is false.
claims.reason: Product differentiation and coefficient extraction establish the identity. At two arity-4 branches and k=3, Delta_3 P=120 while [z^3]E=-54, refuting the stronger sign-cone test only.

claims.statement: For every ordinary path-star with counts a2,a3,a4 of arity-2,3,4 branches, m=a2+a3+a4>=1, N=2a2+3a3+4a4, q=N+1, P=G product_r B_r^(a_r)+z(1+z)^q, and integer-zero-extended forward differences, every natural strict descent k with Delta_k P<0 satisfies 54k>=24N-4a2-3a3-5. Equivalently, with h=(2/3)a2+(1/2)a3, it satisfies 9k+1-4N+h>0. As a count-relaxed corollary, 9k+1-4N+hmax(m,N)>0 where hmax=2m-N/2 for N>=3m and hmax=m-N/6 for N<=3m.
claims.scope: All m>=1 and all counts a2,a3,a4; every strict descent, including the terminal zero-extended descent and in particular the actual least strict descent x. Parent-rank restriction only; no selector, MASS, or payment conclusion.
claims.reason: The coefficientwise D_q^(4)(P)+hP>=0 argument in the shared profile-sensitive candidate proves the exact universal inequality and its hmax corollary informally. It is not Lean-verified.

limitations: The all-profile rank proof is informal and has no Lean award.
The weaker E=(1+z)P'-(N+2)P coefficient-cone route is invalid; its failure is not a counterexample to the rank theorem.
No deletion-selection, selected-mass, payment, or primary-claim conclusion follows from this review.
